claim: A prevailing theory posits that spatial information travels from the postrhinal cortex (POR) to the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC), and nonspatial information is transmitted from the perirhinal cortex (PER) to the lateral entorhinal cortex (LEC), before both types of information merge in the hippocampus.
source: A prevailing theory posits that spatial information travels from the postrhinal cortex (POR) to the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC), and nonspatial information is transmitted from the perirhinal cortex (PER) to the lateral entorhinal cortex (LEC), before both types of information merge in the hippocampus (Knierim et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established theory in the field.

claim: The prevailing theory does not explain explicitly how visual scene information is processed in medial temporal lobe circuits.
source: An important caveat of this theory is that it does not explain explicitly how visual scene information is processed in these circuits, although it becomes increasingly clear that visual scenes may provide critical contextual information to the hippocampus (Dombeck et al., 2010; Hassabis and Maguire, 2009; Kim et al., 2012; Maguire and Mullally, 2013; Prusky et al., 2004; Wirth et al., 2003; Zeidman et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is an inference about the limitations of existing theory, supported by citations.

claim: Visual scenes may provide critical contextual information to the hippocampus.
source: An important caveat of this theory is that it does not explain explicitly how visual scene information is processed in these circuits, although it becomes increasingly clear that visual scenes may provide critical contextual information to the hippocampus (Dombeck et al., 2010; Hassabis and Maguire, 2009; Kim et al., 2012; Maguire and Mullally, 2013; Prusky et al., 2004; Wirth et al., 2003; Zeidman et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The LEC, but not the MEC, is critical when rats were required to manipulate a common object in different ways using visual scenes in the background.
source: Specifically, we found that the LEC, but not the MEC, is critical when rats were required to manipulate a common object in different ways (by pushing it or digging sand) using visual scenes in the background, whereas the MEC, but not the LEC, was important when rats made spatial choices in the T-maze using the same visual scenes.
evidence: The claim is based on findings from a previous study by the authors.

claim: The MEC, but not the LEC, was important when rats made spatial choices in the T-maze using visual scenes.
source: Specifically, we found that the LEC, but not the MEC, is critical when rats were required to manipulate a common object in different ways (by pushing it or digging sand) using visual scenes in the background, whereas the MEC, but not the LEC, was important when rats made spatial choices in the T-maze using the same visual scenes.

claim: The MEC may bias the POR network toward processing incoming sensory inputs in relation to the spatial navigation components of the task.
